name: P7 radar PPI (12DP7 indicator drive: 15 rpm, 1400 pps, 60-mile sweep)

timing.ref: PPI: one pass per antenna rotation (CAA TDR 211: 15 rpm); raster fields kept from the 5151 profile are unused

drive.mapping: level = floor(3 (1 - luma) + 0.5) / 3: dark art drives the beam
drive.ref: MDA video pin = 2/3, intensity pin = 1/3 of the luminance (Wikipedia, IBM Monochrome Display Adapter). Content is free, so the TTL signal may switch anywhere along a line.

ppi.ref: CAA Technical Development Report 211 (Randall & McIntire, 1953), Characteristics of Magnesium Fluoride and P7 Phosphors for Radar PPI Applications: trail test 60-mile sweep, 15 rpm, PRF 1400 pps, 1.0 us pulse; 12DP7 trail 8 scans; dark room
ppi.model: E per pass = drive * r_ref / max(r, spot sigma); hit at azimuth / 2 pi of the rotation (clockwise from the top); light averaged over the last 1/60 s
assumed: sweep radius reaches the panel's corners, centred on the panel

phosphor.efficiency_ref: Tektronix relative luminance (via Jankowiak): P7 45, P4 70
phosphor.persistence_class: blue: medium short (25-75 us); yellow-green: long (400 ms to 10 %)
facts: Phosphor
P7 cascade screen: purplish-blue ZnS:Ag on yellowish-green (Zn,Cd)S:Cu; the beam excites the blue layer, the blue light excites the yellow (RCA 1961; MIT 1948)
Colours (measured)
blue x 0.151 y 0.032, 435 nm; yellow-green x 0.357 y 0.537, 555 nm (RCA TPM-1508A)
Decay (measured)
blue 10 % after 45 us; yellow-green 10 % after 371 ms (RCA 5ABP7 persistence chart, traced)
Late afterglow (assumed)
past the end of RCA's chart, the yellow-green continues at the chart's final slope (0.65 decades per decade)
Colour balance (derived)
blue 4.3 % of the luminance during excitation: the mix closest to white (illuminant C), as RCA describes the screen's fluorescence
Display
the layers mix in linear light; the steady colour lies inside sRGB. Only a colour outside it (the bare blue flash) is moved toward grey at its true luminance
Known gap
P7 is not linear: after 100 ms, a single flash glows longer (MIT 1948), and repeated flashes build up more, than this linear model shows; it follows RCA's steady-excitation decay, which fits a raster
Context
P7 was a radar phosphor; here it is driven by the 5151's raster and spot
Radar drive (measured)
CAA 1953 trail test: 15 rpm scan, 1400 pulses/s, 1 µs pulse, 60-mile sweep, 12DP7 tube, dark room
PPI physics (derived)
each point is passed once per 4 s rotation; 5600 sweeps per rotation overlap everywhere, so the charge per pass falls as 1/radius
Trail (measured)
a moving target's trail stayed visible for 8 scans (32 s) on the 12DP7
What you see
the light of the last 1/60 s (the raster screens average over their refresh instead)
refs: RCA TPM-1508A Phosphors for Cathode-Ray Tubes (Oct 1961): pp. 6-7, 13, 18
W. T. Dyall, A Study of the Persistence Characteristics of Various Cathode Ray Tube Phosphors, MIT RLE Technical Report 56 (1948): Table 3, sections VI-VII

colour.note: Two layers, each with its true linear-sRGB colour per unit luminance (phosphor.layers; negative = outside the display). Mixed per pixel, then brought into the gamut.

spot.ref: Philips M31-336/338/350: about 1300 lines over 201 mm (shrinking raster, 68.5 cd/m2, phosphor W); flat-field pitch = 2 sigma
spot.line_count_height_note: Philips measures the 1300 lines on a 216 x 162 mm raster without saying which height the count refers to; over 162 mm the line width would be 0.125 mm. 201 mm (the useful height) is used.

bloom.model: sigma(drive) = sigma_mm * (drive / efficiency_vs_P4) ** power; drive = beam signal relative to full drive, held at min_drive_fraction or above (the measured currents span a factor of 4)
bloom.ref: Philips T16 1987, Resolution characteristics, Fig. 5 (M31-336..350, 12 kV): line width at 50, 75, 100, 200 uA, traced into tools/philips-m31-line-width.json

raster.note: raster assumed to fill the useful height of a Philips 31 cm 90 degree monitor tube; the 5151's own picture size is not published

faceplate.ref: Philips T16 1987: light transmission about 50 % (normal tint), etched anti-glare option

contrast.note: video gain (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the data')

brightness.note: uniform beam on every line (IBM: 'increases the brightness of the entire screen'); fraction of full drive
